title: fix(#10241): prevent race condition in unique() validation allowing duplicates
notes: DRAFT: built from a manual review of the PR, not yet from benchmark runs; severities are estimates, and `rejected` items are wrong findings anticipated from that review, not ones runs have made. Closed without merging. The issue is referenced only in the title (no closing keyword, so GitHub doesn't link it); it is open, and its thread discusses fixes, including an in-memory claim that is 'released after saveDoc()' (Option A), which a review reading the issue can compare against, but nobody commented on this PR's code. The PR's only comment is a maintainer closing it because the contributor wasn't assigned; there are no reviews or inline comments. The fix doesn't close the race it targets, and the shared lock changes the `exists` validator too.

code-review.notes: `severity` is the severity the finding deserves, estimated from a manual review (no benchmark runs yet). `extra_credit` holds correct findings a review earns credit for but isn't marked down for missing.

required.summary: The lock is released in exists()'s finally, as soon as the DB query returns, but the duplicate isn't in the database until the transitions finish and the doc is saved (saveDoc in shared-libs/transitions, after validation). A second request whose unique() check runs after the first one's check returned, but before its save, takes the lock, finds nothing and passes: exactly the issue's race (checks ~5s apart, saves ~13s after arrival). The lock only catches two checks whose queries overlap in time. The PR's 'Why this works' claims the window between query and save is protected, which is false; the issue's Option A releases the claim after saveDoc().
required.match: Says the lock is released when exists() returns (or after the query), before the document is saved, so a duplicate checked in between still passes. Only saying the lock is per-process is not a match: that is lock-per-process.

required.summary: exists() also backs the `exists` validator (validator_functions.js:66, which checks a referenced report of a given form exists, e.g. that a pregnancy was registered for the patient). With the lock, a concurrent exists() call with the same key returns true without querying, so the second of two concurrent reports referencing the same missing record passes validation even though nothing exists. `return true` means 'found' to that validator.
required.match: Says the lock's `return true` also affects the `exists` validator (or any caller that wants 'exists' to mean a record was found), making it pass without checking the database. Saying only that unique() can be wrongly rejected is in-flight-doc-assumed-valid.

required.summary: A concurrent unique()/uniqueWithin() call reports 'not unique' just because another check with the same values is in flight, without knowing whether that doc will be saved or saved clean. exists() ignores docs that have `errors`, so if the in-flight doc fails another validation (or isn't saved), the second report is still rejected as a duplicate of nothing.
required.match: Says a concurrent check is reported as a duplicate (not unique) even when the in-flight doc may fail validation, have errors or never be saved. Saying the same about the `exists` validator passing is exists-validator-short-circuit.

extra_credit.summary: The lock is a module-level Set, so it only serialises checks within one Node process. It does nothing across API replicas (the issue's instance runs on EKS, and the issue's Option B is for multi-pod), or between API and Sentinel, or the webapp, which each load this library.
extra_credit.match: Says the in-memory lock doesn't work across processes, pods or instances.

extra_credit.summary: No test is added for the lock: nothing exercises concurrent exists() calls, the short-circuit, or the release in finally. The description cites only existing tests passing.
extra_credit.match: Says the new locking behaviour has no tests.

rejected.summary: The has()/add() pair is a check-then-act race: two calls can both see the key absent and both take the lock.
rejected.reason: has() and add() run synchronously with no await between them, so no other call can interleave in a single Node process.
rejected.match: Says two calls can both pass the has() check before either adds the key.

rejected.summary: If the query or allDocs throws, the lock is never released, so later checks for that key always return true.
rejected.reason: Everything after add() is in a try with a finally that deletes the key, so it is released on errors and early returns.
rejected.match: Says the lock stays held if exists() throws or returns early.

rejected.summary: The lock key ignores options.duration, so unique() and uniqueWithin() calls with the same fields collide and give wrong results.
rejected.reason: True that the key ignores duration, but the in-flight doc is current, so it falls within any duration: a uniqueWithin caller treating it as a match is what it would conclude once the doc is saved. The real problems are lock-released-before-save and in-flight-doc-assumed-valid.
rejected.match: Says the missing duration in the lock key makes unique and uniqueWithin give wrong results for each other.

requirements.notes: Reports split and merge requirements differently from run to run, so each item is matched by meaning, and one report item may cover several. `status` is the bucket it should land in; `acceptable` lists other buckets that are not counted as a miss. The issue is referenced only in the title, so a run may not read it; its expected behaviour and the PR's 'Why this works' are the same requirement (concurrent duplicates are rejected). Report items for the Testing bullets (132 tests pass, existing tests still work) match nothing and are not scored. `preconditions_to_confirm` holds the operational facts the skill should list under 'Preconditions to confirm'; empty means it should say None.

required.summary: The issue expects a duplicate report sent while the first is still being processed (seconds apart) to be marked not unique, and the PR claims the lock protects the window between the query and the save. It doesn't: the lock is released when exists() returns, before the first doc is saved, so only checks whose queries overlap are caught (see code-review lock-released-before-save).
required.match: Not delivered because the lock is released before the doc is saved. Delivered, or Not delivered only because the lock is per-process, is a miss.

required.summary: exists() builds a key from the sorted field:value pairs, returns true if another call holds it, otherwise adds it to an in-memory Set and deletes it in a finally after the query.
required.match: A Delivered item for the in-memory lock, its short-circuit to true, or its release in finally. Separate items for these together match.

preconditions_to_confirm.summary: The lock is in-process memory, so it can only work if every unique() check for the same values runs in one API process: a single API instance, not several replicas (the issue's instance runs on EKS).
preconditions_to_confirm.match: Lists running a single API process/instance (no replicas or multiple pods) as something to confirm.

undisclosed_changes.notes: One changed file, walked in full. The description talks only about unique(), but the change is in the shared exists() helper.

required.summary: The lock is in exists(), which also backs the `exists` and `uniqueWithin` validators, so their behaviour changes too; the description presents it as a unique() change only. For `exists`, a concurrent call now passes without querying (see code-review exists-validator-short-circuit).
required.match: Lists the change to the `exists` and/or `uniqueWithin` validators (or to every caller of exists()) as undisclosed.

required.summary: The callback's `doc` is renamed to `rowDoc` (it shadowed the parameter) and the '// filter out docs with errors' comment is removed. Behaviour is unchanged.
required.match: Lists the doc -> rowDoc rename or the removed comment as undisclosed.
